subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Whom did William appoint as Archbishop of Canterbury to reform the English Church?
questions.explain: William appointed Lanfranc as Archbishop of Canterbury in 1070 to reform and Normanise the Church.

questions.q: What was a key Norman change to the Church in England after 1066?
questions.explain: William replaced many English bishops and abbots with Normans, such as Lanfranc as Archbishop.

questions.q: One lasting effect of the Harrying of the North was that the region appeared how in the Domesday Book?
questions.explain: Large parts of the north were recorded as 'waste' in Domesday, reflecting the destruction of 1069-70.

questions.q: Which claimant to the English throne in 1066 was Duke of Normandy?
questions.explain: William, Duke of Normandy, claimed Edward had promised him the throne and invaded in 1066.

questions.q: What type of castle, built quickly from earth and timber, did the Normans first use?
questions.explain: Motte-and-bailey castles, with a mound (motte) and enclosure (bailey), were quick to build after 1066.

questions.q: What was the strong, fortified tower at the centre of a developed Norman castle called?
questions.explain: The keep was the strongly defended central tower, often built in stone, that formed the castle's last stronghold.

questions.q: Where was William crowned King of England on Christmas Day 1066?
questions.explain: William was crowned king at Westminster Abbey on 25 December 1066.

questions.q: At which battle in September 1066 did Harold Godwinson defeat the Norwegian invaders?
questions.explain: Harold defeated Harald Hardrada and Tostig at the Battle of Stamford Bridge in September 1066.

questions.q: In which year was the Domesday Book compiled?
questions.explain: The Domesday Book survey was ordered by William and compiled in 1086.

questions.q: Which northern English battle did Harold's forces lose to the Vikings shortly before Stamford Bridge in 1066?
questions.explain: At the Battle of Fulford in September 1066 the northern earls were defeated by Harald Hardrada's Viking army.

questions.q: Domesday Book recorded an England with roughly what population?
questions.explain: Historians estimate England's population in 1086 was roughly one and a half to two million people.

questions.q: On roughly what date was the Battle of Hastings fought in 1066?
questions.explain: The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066.

questions.q: What service did knights owe their lord in return for land under feudalism?
questions.explain: Knights held land in return for providing military (knight) service to their lord.

questions.q: Tenants-in-chief who received land directly from the king were mostly what after 1066?
questions.explain: William granted most great estates to Norman barons as tenants-in-chief, replacing the Anglo-Saxon elite.

questions.q: Into how many large earldoms was late Anglo-Saxon England mainly divided?
options: Several great earldoms such as Wessex, Mercia and Northumbria
questions.explain: England was divided into powerful earldoms like Wessex, Mercia and Northumbria, ruled by earls under the king.

questions.q: What was the Witan in Anglo-Saxon England?
options: A royal council of nobles and churchmen
questions.explain: The Witan was the council of leading nobles and clergy who advised the Anglo-Saxon king.

questions.q: What was William's brutal campaign to crush rebellion in northern England (1069-70) called?
questions.explain: The Harrying of the North devastated Yorkshire and surrounding regions to suppress resistance.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of the Domesday Book?
options: To record land, ownership and resources for taxation
To plan the invasion of Scotland
questions.explain: The Domesday Book recorded landholding and resources so William could assess wealth and tax.

questions.q: What was a 'thegn' in Anglo-Saxon society around 1060?
options: A local lord who held land and served the king
questions.explain: A thegn was a landholding nobleman below the earls who owed service, including military duty, to the king.

questions.q: Which Anglo-Saxon king died in January 1066, triggering the succession crisis?
questions.explain: Edward the Confessor died childless in January 1066, leaving a disputed succession.

questions.q: In which year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
questions.explain: The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066.

questions.q: Which young Anglo-Saxon, a rival claimant in 1066, was a great-nephew of Edward the Confessor?
questions.explain: Edgar the Aetheling had a strong hereditary claim but was too young and lacked support in 1066.
